issues.problem: Claimed that applying f(x) = 1/(1-x) three times "brings every number back to where it started"; false for x = 1 (not in the domain) and for x = 0 (f(0) = 1, then f(1) is undefined).
issues.fix: Restricted the claim to numbers other than 0 and 1, with the reason.

issues.problem: 26A09 (Elementary functions) classifies work on specific elementary functions (exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, algebraic); it is not the code for the general notion of a function and its graph.

issues.problem: Said injective and bijective maps "make encodings and compression reversible"; vague, and lossless compression maps are not bijections in general.

issues.problem: Read off from a numerical table that "for base e it is exactly 1"; a table cannot show an exact value, and e was defined only as the limit of (1 + 1/n)^n, so this is a theorem the lesson does not prove.
issues.fix: Said the table suggests it and that the exact statement is proved in [[derivative]] / [[diff-rules]].

issues.problem: About 2,430 words, too long for a school-stage lesson; repetition between intro, sections and pitfalls.

issues.problem: Used |sin t| <= |t| without saying where it comes from (it is not a prerequisite fact), and listed sqrt, a^x, log, sin, cos as continuous without saying this is assumed.
issues.fix: Explained |sin t| <= |t| from sin t < t (proved in [[limits]]) and |sin t| <= 1; said the other continuity facts are accepted without proof.

issues.where: section/Bisection, and why the real numbers matter
issues.problem: The IVT proof rests on the least upper bound property, which is not proved in this lesson or in its prerequisite (limits); the text linked [[real-numbers]] without saying it is assumed.
issues.fix: Stated explicitly that the property is an axiom of the real numbers, taken as given, and pointed to [[real-numbers]].

issues.where: example/Half the distance in half the time
issues.problem: Named "the universal chord theorem of Paul Levy" without stating it, and asserted that pace plans with no 24-minute 4 km window exist without giving one; the 1/n generalisation was only gestured at.
issues.fix: Stated the theorem exactly (continuous f on [0,1], f(0) = f(1), horizontal chord of length 1/n for every positive integer n, not necessarily for other lengths), showed how the runner problem is the case f(s) = d(60s) - 10s, spelled out the n-piece argument, and gave an explicit increasing pace plan d(t) = 19t/120 + (1/2)sin^2(pi t/24) whose every 24-minute window covers exactly 3.8 km.

issues.problem: About 2,330 words, too long for a school-stage lesson; the extreme value theorem was restated in the pitfalls and bisection was described three times.
issues.fix: Trimmed every block (to about 1,900 words including the added universal chord material); all definitions, proofs and examples kept.

issues.problem: 26A03 (Foundations: limits and generalizations, elementary topology of the line) is the code for the limits concept; continuity and the intermediate value theorem belong to 26A15.
issues.fix: Removed 26A03; kept 26A15.

issues.problem: Said Peano guarantees "a local solution of y' = f(x, y) whenever f is continuous"; the theorem is about an initial value problem and needs continuity near the initial point, and gives no uniqueness.
issues.fix: Restated with the initial condition, local continuity hypothesis and the non-uniqueness caveat.
